manifest_entry.statement: Assume AC_omega. For R>0 and n>=2 let S^n_R be the round sphere of radius R in R^(n+1) with the induced metric. Then S^n_R is a compact connected complete boundaryless Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature 1/R^2; the maximal geodesic with gamma(0)=p, gamma'(0)=v is gamma(t)=cos(|v|t/R)p+(R/|v|)sin(|v|t/R)v for v nonzero (constant for v=0); d_g(x,y)=R arccos(<x,y>/R^2), with diameter pi R attained exactly at antipodal pairs; and for unit v the cut time is c_p(v)=pi R, Cut(p)={-p}, inj(p)=pi R and exp_p is injective on the open tangent ball of radius pi R.
manifest_entry.strategy: Project the ambient derivative to get the Levi-Civita connection, integrate the geodesic ODE in closed form, use Hopf-Rinow for the minimizing direction of the distance formula, and read the cut time and injectivity radius off the distance formula.
manifest_entry.title: Round sphere model geometry

manifest_entry.statement: Assume AC_omega. For a>0 let U^n={y>0} in R^n carry g_a=(a^2y^2)^(-1) sum dx^i dx^i. Then g_a is a Riemannian metric and (U^n,g_a) is a complete simply connected boundaryless n-manifold of constant sectional curvature -a^2; the vertical lines t->(x_0,y_0e^(at)) and the Euclidean semicircles centred on y=0 are unit-speed geodesics defined on all of R, and every maximal geodesic is one of them.
manifest_entry.strategy: Compute the Christoffel symbols of the conformal factor, evaluate the coordinate curvature formula to get R(X,Y)Z=-a^2(g(Y,Z)X-g(X,Z)Y), exhibit vertical lines and semicircles as complete unit-speed geodesics, show they cover every initial datum, and use convexity of the half-space plus Hopf-Rinow.
manifest_entry.title: Upper half-space model geometry

manifest_entry.statement: Assume AC_omega. For n>=1 let Z^n act on R^n by translations and let T^n=R^n/Z^n carry the quotient metric g with q^*g the Euclidean metric. Then (T^n,g) is a connected boundaryless complete Riemannian n-manifold, q is a surjective local isometry, the curvature vanishes for n>=2, and the quotient charts identify T_[x]T^n with R^n so the maximal geodesic with initial datum v is t->[x+tv] and exp_[x](v)=[x+v]; hence exp_[x](0)=exp_[x](e_1) and exp_[x] is not injective.
manifest_entry.strategy: Covering boxes give a smooth atlas and the Hausdorff second-countable quotient; translations make the Euclidean metric descend along the local isometry q; straight lines push to complete geodesics; constant-coefficient charts have zero curvature; and exp_[x](e_1)=exp_[x](0).
manifest_entry.title: Flat torus model geometry

manifest_entry.statement: For a finite positive Borel measure μ on C, supp μ is the complement of the union of all open sets V with μ(V)=0; it is closed, it is the smallest closed set carrying μ, μ is carried by a compact set exactly when supp μ is compact, and μ≠0 exactly when supp μ≠∅.
manifest_entry.strategy: Define the support as the complement of the union of all open null sets; use the countable rational-box basis to show that this union is null without any choice principle, so the support is the smallest closed carrier, and record the nonempty, carried-by-compact and compact-support conventions.
manifest_entry.title: Support of a finite Borel measure on the plane

manifest_entry.proof_strategy: Biholomorphic pullback preserves upper semicontinuity and the failure of being identically -infinity on components. For the harmonic-comparison form of subharmonicity, conjugate a candidate majorant h on a disc by the inverse biholomorphism; the resulting plane harmonic function H has the same boundary domination, and the maximum principle applied to u∘G-H forces the comparison to hold inside. Apply the implication in both directions using G and G^{-1}.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Class Notes Math 618: Complex Variables II, Spring 2016, §7.2 (standard ways to produce subharmonic functions: u∘f for u subharmonic and f holomorphic)

manifest_entry.statement: Let $G:\Omega_1\to\Omega_2$ be a biholomorphism of complex domains. A function $u:\Omega_2\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is subharmonic on $\Omega_2$ if and only if $u\circ G$ is subharmonic on $\Omega_1$.
manifest_entry.title: Plane subharmonicity is invariant under biholomorphic change of coordinate

manifest_entry.proof_strategy: Reduce the plane statement to the harmonic-majorant characterisation: on a closed disc the difference u-h is upper semicontinuous, so its finite maximum over the compact disc is attained; the harmonic-comparison obligation follows from the maximum principle on the open disc, whose maximum set is clopen in a connected neighbourhood on which u is subharmonic. The surface statement is chartwise, using that subharmonicity on a surface is defined chartwise and invariant under biholomorphic change of coordinate.

manifest_entry.statement: Plane domains: an upper semicontinuous function on a complex domain that is subharmonic on a connected open neighbourhood of each of its points is subharmonic. Riemann surfaces: an upper semicontinuous function on an open subset of a Riemann surface that is subharmonic on an open neighbourhood of each of its points is subharmonic. No choice principle is used.
manifest_entry.title: Locality of subharmonicity in the plane and on Riemann surfaces

manifest_entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be bounded and open, with nonempty boundary. Suppose $U\supset\overline D$ is open, $\rho\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$, $D=\{\rho<0\}$ in $U$, and $\rho$ is strictly plurisubharmonic near $\partial D$. No nonvanishing-gradient condition is imposed.

For every open $O$ with $\overline D\subset O\subset U$, there are finitely many pairwise disjoint bounded domains $G_1,\ldots,G_N$ such that
$$\overline D\subset G:=\bigcup_{i=1}^N G_i,\qquad \overline G\subset O,$$
each $G_i$ has $C^\infty$ strongly pseudoconvex boundary, and each $G_i$ admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion.
manifest_entry.title: Positive smooth collars for strictly plurisubharmonic negative sets

references.locator: §3.6.4, Theorem 64(1), printed p. 74: exponential improvement of a defining function. The smooth globalization from smooth local data is proved explicitly here.

manifest_entry.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a bounded domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, strongly pseudoconvex at every boundary point. Then there are a neighborhood $U$ of $\overline D$ and $\rho\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ with $D=\{\rho<0\}$ in $U$, $d\rho\ne0$ on $\partial D$, and $\rho$ strictly plurisubharmonic near $\partial D$.
manifest_entry.title: Smooth global defining functions for strongly pseudoconvex boundaries

manifest_entry.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a bounded domain with a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion $S$. Then $\Omega$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex: $-\log\delta_\Omega$ is plurisubharmonic, where $\delta_\Omega$ is the equal-radius polydisc boundary function.
manifest_entry.title: A smooth psh exhaustion gives Hartogs pseudoconvexity on bounded domains

manifest_entry.statement: Every irreducible germ q in the holomorphic UFD O_{ℂⁿ,0} is prime: if q divides a product ab, then q divides a or q divides b.
manifest_entry.strategy: Assume q divides ab with neither factor divisible by q; the cofactor is a nonzero nonunit, and uniqueness of irreducible factorisation applied to ab=qc forces q to be associate to a factor of a or of b, a contradiction.
manifest_entry.title: Irreducible holomorphic germs are prime

manifest_entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through the valuative criterion for proper
morphisms and the universal closedness of finite morphisms. Let $h:X\to Y$ be
a finite morphism of schemes and let $g:Y\to S$ be a proper morphism. Then the
composite $g\circ h:X\to S$ is proper. The same argument gives that a
composite of a finite morphism with a separated morphism is separated, and a
composite of finite-type morphisms is finite type; these two auxiliary facts
are proved as steps below because the composite is not assumed separated in
advance.
manifest_entry.title: Composite of a finite morphism and a proper morphism is proper
